PullRequest.Title: Fix CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT in custom agent hooks
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- resolve format-specific plugin-root variables in hooks declared by plugin-provided custom agents
- centralize plugin-root token/environment metadata across MCP and hook interpolation
- shell-quote plugin roots in command, Bash, and PowerShell hook fields
- add Claude and Open Plugin regression coverage at the custom-agent discovery boundary

## Evidence

### Before fix

The plugin-provided custom agent reaches the participant with a literal `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` token and no `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` environment value.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21fc162b-7847-4806-95cf-d321147da5f9

### After fix

The same scenario resolves both the hook command and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` environment value to the contributing Claude plugin directory. This recording is from the current PR head.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9091f6fc-d31f-4ba0-a886-eae5f86502a3

Both recordings are captioned UI scenarios captured on Code OSS Dev 1.140.0 (macOS arm64). All scenario steps passed; none were skipped or required manual validation.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentPlugins/common/pluginParsers.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/hookSchema.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsServiceImpl.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsService.test.ts`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsService.test.ts --grep 'PromptsService getCustomAgents'`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentPlugins/test/common/pluginParsers.test.ts --grep 'parseHooksJson|plugin root'`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/promptSyntax/hookSchema.test.ts --grep 'parseSubagentHooksFromYaml'`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/plugins/agentPluginFormatDetection.test.ts --grep 'PLUGIN_ROOT expansion in hook commands'`
- before/fixed UI scenarios on Code OSS Dev 1.140.0 (macOS arm64)

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold and warm custom-agent discovery used by agent selection, validation, chat setup, and subagent invocation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold or invalidated cache, listPromptFiles, user-home resolution, every queued agent parse, hook frontmatter parsing, and source-folder diagnostics complete before getCustomAgents resolves. Warm calls reuse CachedPromise and only project the cached discovery results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt files and read/parse each agent markdown file when no live text model supplies it
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold pass: source discovery plus at most one agent-file read per discovered agent, with effective concurrency capped at 10; warm cache: zero reads
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery and per-agent reads were already performed before the diff with the same shared limiter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All cold-pass reads must settle before getCustomAgents resolves; warm calls bypass them

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All visible agent files A; the changed plugin lookup applies only to plugin agents that contain allowed hook frontmatter H and scans the cached plugin array P, adding O(H*P) URI comparisons. Hook interpolation additionally walks each affected hook command object once. File reads remain O(A).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Agent parse/file-read tasks share the service-wide Limiter capped at 10, including across overlapping invalidated passes. The new plugin lookup and interpolation execute synchronously inside those bounded tasks and do not add parallel boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CachedPromise coalesces concurrent callers and retains successful discovery until agent files/models, plugin agent contributions, hook configuration, trust, or lockdown state invalidates it. The plugin observable is actively observed and cached; warm discovery calls perform none of the new lookup/interpolation work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path, O(H*P) lookup, one-pass interpolation, cache lifetime, and 10-task limiter based on the changed hunk and surrounding implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installations can vary from a few agents/plugins to large managed collections, but the newly added CPU work remains small relative to the unchanged file discovery/parsing and is eliminated on warm cache hits. No evidence establishes user-visible latency from the O(H*P) comparisons.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds only cache-recompute-scoped URI comparisons and linear hook-object transformation; it introduces no filesystem/IPC/network fan-out and does not defeat the existing discovery cache or limiter.

Scenarios.Scenario: Claude/Open Plugin hook JSON discovery and reload
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On plugin discovery or a watched manifest/hook change, format detection, manifest/component resolution, the first valid hook JSON read, interpolation, and parsing complete before that plugin's hook observable updates. Subsequent consumers read the observable result off this discovery path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Detect plugin format, read manifest, and read candidate hook JSON files until the first valid definition
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per plugin refresh: existing format/manifest reads and sequential hook-path attempts, stopping at the first valid JSON; warm observable reads perform no file access
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same format, manifest, and hook-file reads occurred before the diff; only in-memory interpolation metadata and cloning changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the plugin's parsed hooks become available, but unchanged by the diff

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of discovered plugins P, candidate hook paths per plugin, and total hook JSON size/command count C. The changed helper adds a deep clone of each command subtree before the existing whole-JSON clone, so allocation remains linear in C rather than changing boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Plugin sources are built serially by _discoverAndBuildPlugins; candidate hook paths for one plugin are tried sequentially until the first valid file. Component observables may resolve independently, but the diff adds no promise, queue, or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-plugin component observables recompute initially and when their watched component paths or manifest change. There is no repeated parsing on ordinary warm reads. Failed candidate paths are retried only on discovery/component refresh as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that interpolation now clones command subtrees and that the existing parser clones the whole JSON, while all filesystem placement, cache invalidation, and concurrency remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Hook configurations are typically small; exceptionally large hook JSON would incur additional linear temporary allocation, but there is no evidence of a realistic size that would create material CPU/GC impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The extra allocation is a bounded linear pass over configuration data on discovery/reload, not unbounded retention, repeated warm-path work, or added I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Executing plugin-agent hooks during a subagent session or tool lifecycle event
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The selected agent's hooks are merged into the subagent request; when a matching lifecycle event fires, configured hook commands are spawned and awaited sequentially. Hook subprocesses are on the lifecycle event's critical path, but interpolation itself occurred earlier during cached discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn /bin/sh or cmd.exe for each configured hook command and await completion
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one subprocess per configured command for each matching event, executed sequentially; unchanged by this diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, the same hook entries produced the same number and sequencing of subprocesses; plugin-root tokens were merely unresolved in the affected custom-agent case.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each spawned command can block the matching hook event until completion or timeout

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of configured commands for the fired hook type K and number of lifecycle events E, yielding up to K subprocesses per event with early return for parsed output where applicable. The diff changes command strings/environment values only and does not change K, E, ordering, or timeout.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Commands in a hook list are executed sequentially; the diff does not add parallel spawning, a new event subscription, or an additional execution path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Agent hook definitions come from cached custom-agent discovery and global plugin hooks from component observables. Cold discovery may precede first use; repeated events reuse parsed definitions. No new positive/negative cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the merge path and executor implementation that metadata interpolation does not create or duplicate hook commands.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual subprocess duration and event frequency depend on user-provided hooks, but cardinality and scheduling are unchanged, so this uncertainty does not indicate a diff-caused regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR corrects command/environment values without increasing subprocess count, serialization, concurrency, or critical-path placement.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and all diff pages. Traced custom-agent discovery, plugin hook refresh, and runtime hook execution, including caches, bounded concurrency, filesystem reads, and subprocess cardinality. The diff adds small cache-scoped CPU/allocation work but no actionable performance regression, and it does not itself fix a proven shipped performance regression.
